blocks.html: Women have this peculiar to them, says the Philosopher, that they believe lightly, and are easy to be deceived by the ruses and wiles of men a.

notes.citation: Aristotle, History of Animals IX, at the opening (IX.1, 608b: the female is "more easily deceived", εὐαπατητότερον); the print's de natura auiũ, "of the nature of birds", is a wrong sort or slip for animalium
notes.original: Ariſtote au cõmencement du ix. liu. de natura auiũ.
notes.gloss: Book IX opens with the characters of the two sexes: the female softer, more jealous, more querulous, more shameless, more false of speech, more easily deceived and of better memory.

blocks.html: Such, to be sure, was the nature of the men of old: to deceive the female kind, those credulous hearts <sup class="mk" data-key="b" data-page="p102">b</sup>.

notes.citation: Publio Fausto Andrelini (Faustus, of Forlì, c. 1462–1518), Livia (the Amores), book IV as cited — the couplet not located (no searchable text of the Livia)
notes.gloss: The couplet: Scilicet ista fuit veterum natura virorum, / fallere femineum, credula corda, genus. Andrelini's Livia, an elegiac collection in four books (Paris, 1490), was a school text in France in Coras's youth; the line and its place in book IV are unverified.

blocks.html: And the Emperor Justinian said: we have sufficiently known the feeble nature of women, subject to a thousand trickeries and circumventions <sup class="mk" data-key="c" data-page="p102">c</sup>.

notes.citation: Novels (the Authenticum), collation 7, the title De aequalitate dotis et propter nuptias donationis (Nov. 97), at the paragraph Quaesitum (cf. Nov. 97.3, Quaesitum est igitur, followed by Infirmitatem namque muliebris naturae et satis novimus et quia facile circumventiones fiunt adversus eas)
notes.original: P. quæſitũ. de æqua dor. aux nouuelles ſous la collation vij.
notes.gloss: De æqua dor. = De aequalitate dotis; the P. is the print's sort for §. Justinian's legislation on the dowry repeatedly pleads the weakness of women and their exposure to deception as its ground.
